thread:
Maya: Ran an nsys trace on the nightly prefix-cache job. Seeing a repeating latency oscillation when warmup traffic hits ~30% reuse.
Sam: Can you paste the NVTX timeline or a quick snapshot? :thinking:
Maya: Pasted a short snippet from the timeline, the pattern is: burst of optimized GEMM kernels -> small fallback kernels -> optimized again. Happens every ~200ms for a few seconds.
Maya: Example nvtx region names: OPT_GEMM, GEMM_FALLBACK, KV_LOOKUP, DISPATCH.
Kevin: Huh. That looks like kernel selection thrash. Do we have the kernel selection logs for those requests?
Maya: Yes — attached extract from the runtime log (sanitized):
```
[req=2345] seqlen=128 prefix_hit=true cached_kv=78 -> select OPT_GEMM
[req=2346] seqlen=8 prefix_hit=false cached_kv=0 -> select GEMM_FALLBACK
[req=2347] seqlen=64 prefix_hit=true cached_kv=12 -> select OPT_GEMM
```
Maya: Notice the same model and similar seqlens but different kernel picks.
Ciara: Could be kernel score instability because of input batch composition. Are we batching by arrival vs affinity?
Sam: Nightly config is arrival-batching with a 25ms aggregation window, with small affinity hints off.
Kevin: That explains it — mixed small and medium sequences in same batch can flip kernel heuristics. Suggest testing staggered batching + prefer-affinity to keep hot prefixes together.
Maya: I tried a narrow experiment: forced affinity and 50ms window, re-ran nsys. Oscillation reduced but KV_LOOKUP latency spiked slightly.
Maya: nvtx extract:
```
Time 0ms: KV_LOOKUP (2.3ms)
Time 1ms: OPT_GEMM (6.1ms)
Time 3ms: KV_LOOKUP (1.9ms)
Time 4ms: GEMM_FALLBACK (12.4ms)
```
Ciara: So warmup causes partial cache population, some requests hit heavy KV entries causing different dispatch paths. Maybe the KV cache warmup strategy is doing prefix writes in parallel causing eviction churn.
Sam: Related note: I saw metric 'kv_write_rate' spike at same time as oscillation. Could be write-thrashing evictions.
Kevin: Two hypotheses: 1) kernel-selection scoring relies on recent batch statistics and jitter swings it; 2) KV cache writes during warmup evict hot prefixes leading to smaller cached_kv and fallback picks.
Maya: I also captured a perfetto trace with CPU timeline + GPU NVTX. Link: perfetto://trace/abc123 (sanitized). In perfetto you can see CPU thread doing cache writes every ~50ms aligned with the oscillation.
Ciara: Can we try throttling background cache-writes during warmup (lower concurrency) and enable stable kernel scoring (add hysteresis to kernel choice)?
Sam: I can run two quick A/B experiments on staging: (A) reduce cache write concurrency from 8->2, keep current batching; (B) add kernel scoring hysteresis (require 2 consistent samples before switching).
Maya: Please run both. If (A) reduces kv_write_rate and oscillation disappears, we keep (A). If (B) helps but adds tail latency, we might combine.
perf-bot: Submitted perf job #472 with both configs. Traces will be at s3://redwood-perf/nightly/472/ (will post link when ready). :white_check_mark:
Kevin: One more ask — add logging of 'last_kernel_choice' and 'kernel_score' in a compact CSV for the affected period so we can correlate with kv_hit_count.
Maya: Will do. I'll also export a small script to parse the nsys timeline and produce a kernel-switch histogram.
Sam: Thanks team. Plan: wait for job results, analyze CSVs and perfetto, then iterate on batching heuristics and cache-writer backoff.
Ciara: If anyone sees the oscillation elsewhere, ping me. Might be relevant to Dedicated customers with mixed slice workloads. :eyes:
Maya: Uploaded initial CSVs to the debug bucket: s3://redwood-debug/prefetch-osc/172500/
Sam: Got them, starting analysis.
Kevin: Nice! If we can stabilize kernel choice during warmup, we should document the heuristic change and add a fallback that preserves latency SLOs.
Maya: Agreed. Will open a lightweight RFC once we have A/B results.
